intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 (SPGFX3) is caused by hemizygous mutation in the CFAP47 gene on chromosome Xp21.1.

checks.claim: X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 (SPGFX3) is caused by hemizygous mutation in the CFAP47 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: our experimental observations in humans and mice demonstrate that hemizygous mutations in CFAP47 can induce X-linked MMAF and asthenoteratozoospermia
checks.explanation: The paper does not use the label SPGFX3, which is OMIM's name for the disorder. It does state that hemizygous CFAP47 mutations cause X-linked MMAF and asthenoteratozoospermia.

checks.claim: The CFAP47 gene is located on chromosome Xp21.1.
checks.evidence_quote: permitted the identification of a hemizygous Xp21.1 deletion removing the entire CFAP47 gene
checks.explanation: An Xp21.1 deletion that removes the whole gene places CFAP47 at Xp21.1.

paragraphs.text: X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 is a form of primary male infertility marked by asthenoteratozoospermia with multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagella (MMAF) (Liu et al., 2021).

checks.claim: X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 is a form of primary male infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: Deleterious variants in X-linked CFAP47 induce asthenoteratozoospermia and primary male infertility.
checks.explanation: The title calls the condition primary male infertility.

checks.claim: X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 is characterized by asthenoteratozoospermia with multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagella (MMAF).
checks.evidence_quote: hemizygous mutations in CFAP47 can induce X-linked MMAF and asthenoteratozoospermia
checks.explanation: The paper links CFAP47 to asthenoteratozoospermia with MMAF.

paragraphs.text: Liu et al. (2021) studied 3 unrelated Chinese men with MMAF and a man from an Australian cohort of men with severe asthenoteratozoospermia. All of the men showed typical MMAF phenotypes and had primary infertility.

checks.evidence_quote: WES data from an additional cohort of severe asthenoteratozoospermic men originating from Australia permitted the identification of a hemizygous Xp21.1 deletion removing the entire CFAP47 gene.
checks.explanation: One man from the Australian cohort was identified.

checks.claim: All of the men with CFAP47-related infertility studied by Liu et al. (2021) showed typical MMAF phenotypes.
checks.evidence_quote: All men harboring hemizygous CFAP47 variants displayed typical MMAF phenotypes.

checks.claim: All of the men with CFAP47-related infertility studied by Liu et al. (2021) had primary infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: Deleterious variants in X-linked CFAP47 induce asthenoteratozoospermia and primary male infertility.
checks.explanation: Primary male infertility appears only in the title, as a general statement. The abstract does not say that each of the four men had primary infertility; that detail may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

paragraphs.text: Liu et al. (2021) used whole-exome sequencing to study 3 unrelated Chinese men with MMAF. Each man was hemizygous for a missense variant in the X-linked CFAP47 gene. None of the 3 variants was found in human control population genome databases, and several bioinformatic tools predicted all 3 to be deleterious. Immunoblotting and immunofluorescence showed clearly reduced levels of CFAP47 in spermatozoa from all 3 men. In whole-exome data from another cohort of men with severe asthenoteratozoospermia from Australia, Liu et al. (2021) found a man with a hemizygous Xp21.1 deletion that removed the entire CFAP47 gene.

paragraphs.text: Liao et al. (2022) screened 7 men with MMAF for mutations. In 1 of them they found 2 novel mutations in CFAP47: c.706G-A, which causes a val236-to-met (V236M) substitution, and c.1337C-T, which causes a thr446-to-met (T446M) substitution. Immunoblotting and immunofluorescence showed that CFAP47 was greatly reduced in this man's spermatozoa. WDR87 expression was also much lower, with weak signals next to the sperm nuclei. Liao et al. (2022) also showed that CFAP47 interacted with WDR87 in the midpiece of the sperm flagellum. They concluded that CFAP47 is needed to transport WDR87 during the biogenesis of the sperm flagellum.

paragraphs.text: Liu et al. (2021) found that adult male Cfap47-mutated mice were sterile. Their sperm had reduced motility and abnormal flagellar shape and movement. Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) restored fertility in these mice.
